root_cause.text: The use of `pskb_pull()` on cloned, coalesced TCP stream skbs in `ovpn_tcp_rcv` could cause an integer overflow when the data offset (skb->data - skb->head) exceeds the u16 capacity of `skb->network_header`, leading to a subsequent failure of `skb_reset_network_header` and packet drops.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states: "Using pskb_pull with large offsets on coalesced skbs causes skb->data - skb->head to exceed the u16 storage of skb->network_header. This causes skb_reset_network_header to fail on the inner decapsulated packet, resulting in packet drops." The patch removes the `pskb_pull` call and instead allocates a new skb using `skb_copy_bits` to extract the packet content without adjusting the original skb.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor TCP packet reception to copy packet into a new skb instead of modifying the original, fixing potential skb issues and adding early length check.
intent_record.what: Added a new helper function ovpn_tcp_skb_packet that allocates a new skb and copies the packet data from the original skb, consuming it. Modified ovpn_tcp_rcv to use this helper, removed in-place skb pull/trim, and added an early length check.
intent_record.how: Instead of modifying the original skb in place (which could affect other references), the code now creates a separate skb for the packet data, ensuring safe skb lifecycle and allowing early validation of packet length before any skb manipulation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing packet length header write in TCP receive path by storing pkt_len in the two-byte header before sending to userspace.
intent_record.what: Changed from skb_push(skb, 2) to *(__be16 *)__skb_push(skb, sizeof(u16)) = htons(pkt_len); to write the packet length into the pushed header bytes.
intent_record.how: Now the two-byte header before the data contains the correct packet length in network byte order, whereas previously only space was reserved without writing the length.

bic_trace_step.reason: In ovpn_tcp_rcv, the code calls pskb_pull(skb, off) (line 'if (!pskb_pull(skb, off))'). This is the vulnerable construct: pskb_pull on a potentially cloned/coalesced skb can cause an integer overflow when skb->data - skb->head exceeds u16 capacity of skb->network_header, leading to skb_reset_network_header failure. No fix or subsequent handling is present in this commit; it introduces the vulnerability.
